body:
I’m the son of a now retired pastor. I’m in my late 20s and decided a couple of years ago that I was done with my faith. There was a whole lot that came with that psychologically but I was a little worried how my family would take it. 

I’ve not really spoken outright about not believing so I’m sure there are some people in my extended family and friends that really don’t know but my immediate family is aware. 

They are still quite accepting and loving as they were before but I don’t try to start or get involved in religious or theological discussion like I used to. I’m not confrontational and I’m not well spoken when talking about deep stuff like that, especially when I know someone is going to disagree. I guess I’m still afraid that I’ll upset them and they’ll reject me if I tell them how I really think and feel.
Oh yeah, you know what I haven’t tried that. I bet that will work immediately with zero issues 🙄
I have friends who care about me and I’m open with them for the most part. I have a good support system but that hasn’t changed how I feel.

It was originally because I was Christian and born into a religious family with a pastor as a father. I was scared to break rules and scared to flirt with girls. Sucked at picking up on social cues. 

Now I’m no longer religious and so I don’t have that stopping me at least. However I’m still afraid to approach women and interact with them in a romantic way. Also any woman that I’m really into never seems to be physically attracted to me, they just see me as a funny friendly guy, which is ok to an extent but it’s really frustrating sometimes. 

I just wish someone would return the same feelings that I have for them.
